newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Brent steady, NYMEX retraces some losses.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Brent steady, NYMEX retraces some losses.

text.p: Brent crude futures were untraded at midday on Thursday in Asia, taking its steady cue from modest gains on NYMEX.
August Brent crude futures on SIMEX were quoted at $17.70/$17.85 after London fell 31 cents to $17.77 per barrel on Wednesday.
The London market also opened a chart gap on the front month between $18.02, the low on Tuesday and $17.98, the high of Wednesday.
Traders said the upside appears limited to Wednesday's high, or between $17.50-$18.00, despite worries over delays to Iraqi oil sales.
An unnamed Iraqi UN official said on Wednesday that Iraq would not export any more oil until money set aside for food and humanitarian goods contracts was spent.
NYMEX July, which expires on Friday in New York, was last traded on ACCESS at $18.82 per barrel, up three cents from New York, while August was last traded at $19.01, up five.
Brokers attributed the slight gains to a retracement of some of New York's 44 cent July and 39 cent August losses.
